in_sanskrit.name: राणजित
in_sanskrit.meaning: राण (rāṇa) + जित (jit) = राजा (rājā) + जित (jit) = राजित् (rājit) = ruler + victorious = conquering ruler
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who conquers or rules

in_hindi.name: रानाजित
in_hindi.meaning: राण (rāṇa) + जित (jit) = राजा (rājā) + जित (jit) = राजित् (rājit) = राजा जित (rājā jit) = king + victorious = conquering king
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who conquers or rules as a king

in_tamil.name: ராநாஜித்
in_tamil.meaning: ராணம் (rāṇam) + ஜித் (jit) = ராஜா (rājā) + ஜித் (jit) = ராஜித் (rājith) = ராஜா ஜித் (rājā jith) = ஜீவத்மிக்கு விக்கியத்தில் விடும் பெரிய வீரன் (jīvathmikku vikkyathill vidum periya veēraṉ) = a mighty warrior who rules over a living being
in_tamil.long_meaning: A mighty warrior who rules over a living being

in_telugu.name: రానాజిట్
in_telugu.meaning: రాణము (rāṇamu) + జిత్ (jit) = రాజా (rājā) + జిత్ (jit) = రాజిట్ (rājita) = రాజజిత్ (rājajit) = జీవదేశపేద్దళే వీరుడు (jīvadēśapēddalē vēruḍu) = a mighty warrior who rules over a living being
in_telugu.long_meaning: A mighty warrior who rules over a living being

in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Judge of the people

data.cultural_impact: The name Ranajit suggests power, authority, and leadership. In Hindu culture, the name is attributed to royalty and those who hold high positions of power and influence in society. The name evokes a sense of respect, honor, and dignity. In traditional Hindu societies, the title "Rana" or "Raj" has been used to address rulers, chieftains, and leaders who hold significant power and responsibilities. The name signifies a strong and capable leader who commands respect and obedience from the people.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ranajit holds a deeper significance. It suggests that the person bearing this name is entrusted with the responsibilities of guiding, protecting, and leading the people towards spiritual growth and enlightenment. As a spiritual leader, Ranajit is expected to be just, compassionate, and wise, using his power and influence for the betterment of the society and the greater good. The name signifies the idea of taking on the burdens of the world and working towards creating a harmonious and enlightened society. In this way, the name Ranajit holds both worldly and spiritual significance, emphasizing the importance of leadership and service to the community.

historical_references.reference: Ranajit Singh was a prominent Sikh ruler of the Punjab region in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. He began his military career at a young age under the tutelage of Zorawar Singh, a powerful Sikh general. After Zorawar's death, Ranajit rose to power and defeated the Afghan invaders, leading to the establishment of the Sikh Empire in 1799.
historical_references.context: Maharaja of the Sikh Empire in Punjab

historical_references.reference: Ranajit Guha is a renowned Indian historian who has made significant contributions to the field of subaltern studies. His most famous work, 'A Subaltern Studies Reader: Writings from the Indian Anticolonial Intellectual Tradition', was published in 1982. Guha's work has been influential in helping to shift the focus of historical research towards the experiences and perspectives of marginalized groups in Indian society.
